source.title: NeurIPS 2020 Competition: Predicting Generalization in Deep Learning
source.authors: Yiding Jiang; Pierre Foret; Scott Yak; Daniel M. Roy; H. Mobahi; G. Dziugaite; Samy Bengio; Suriya Gunasekar; Isabelle M Guyon; Behnam Neyshabur

record.tranche_reason: The study reports an empirical association between training hyperparameters and out-of-sample accuracy, but does not report the specific comparisons or directions asserted by the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper says models with the same architecture and regularization can differ in test accuracy depending on optimizer, learning rate, or batch size. It does not report result rows comparing random and natural labels, width regimes, convolutional and fully connected networks, adaptive and SGD optimizers, or fixed-epoch large- and small-batch outcomes.
record.test_reason: This competition description reports no results testing V1–V8. Its aggregate observation of test-accuracy variation does not identify optimizer or batch-size directions, and its proposed complexity-measure evaluation does not report sharpness results.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the architecture-selection observation, but not the paper's main purpose. The authors propose a competition and evaluation framework for complexity measures that rank trained networks by generalization gap across hyperparameter, architecture, and dataset changes; this text reports no competition outcomes.
record.recipe_differences: The paper describes a competition and its model dataset rather than testing one of the claim's interventions or measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper says out-of-sample accuracy depends on optimizer, learning rate, and batch size.

fits_no_version.finding: The organizers report test-accuracy differences of up to 20% between models with the same architecture and regularization and 100% training accuracy, depending on optimizer, learning rate, or batch size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Interpolating image classifiers can differ substantially in held-out accuracy when training hyperparameters vary despite matching architecture and regularization.

record.problems: The stated accuracy difference is an aggregate qualitative result without individual model or setting values, direction of effect, uncertainty, or reported controls.
record.rows_left_out: No other outcome on the claim's subject is reported as a result. The tasks and hyperparameter ranges in Section 1.3 describe the competition dataset and setup, not measured outcomes.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance compared with natural-label training.
Test-error changes with width beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD held-out performance under limited or broader tuning and recovery recipes.
Directional large-batch penalties under fixed epoch budgets and their removal through adapted recipes.
Dropout's effects on held-out error across data sizes, dropout strengths, and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware sharpness correlations with generalization gaps and comparison with norm- or margin-based measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Hyperparameter ranges and training budgets describe the benchmark setup, not measured intervention effects. References to prior generalization-measure studies do not constitute this study's own evidence for V7.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and test accuracy versus natural-label generalization.
Test-error behavior as width increases beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected test error and the effects of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD held-out performance, including tuning and recovery conditions.
Large versus small batch held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness or comparisons of generalization-gap measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.

rows.subject: models with the same architecture and regularization (aggregate; individual model names not stated)
rows.operation_detail: Compared out-of-sample accuracy across optimizer, learning-rate, and batch-size choices.
rows.value: sometime up to 20% of test accuracy difference
rows.note: Aggregate qualitative report; the paper does not give the individual comparisons or specify which choices produce higher or lower test accuracy.
rows.check: Section 1.3 identifies the architecture families as VGG-like and Network in Network. The reported difference of up to 20% is an aggregate empirical observation motivating architecture selection, without identified model pairs, baseline accuracies, or directions attributable to optimizer, learning rate, or batch size. It cannot establish any version's effect.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
